description: Reference-based BLASTn classifier that assesses the fraction of a contig matching a curated phage genome database.
algorithmic_approach: Alignment-based classification using mean BLASTn identity and coverage against a phage reference set.
rationale_for_inclusion: Represents the simplest reference-based baseline and the only non-machine-learning tool in routine use for metagenomic phage identification (Jurtz et al., 2016).
non_default_flags: None (bundled ALL_140821_hr phage database specified explicitly via -d)

description: Reference-based MinHash k-mer sketching tool that estimates containment of query contigs in a user-supplied viral signature database.
algorithmic_approach: MinHash-sketch containment search against a user-supplied reference index.
rationale_for_inclusion: Represents the database-dependent class in which novel-sequence detection scales with reference completeness; informative for benchmarking coverage of the vaginal virome.
non_default_flags: Custom phages.sbt.zip reference index curated for this benchmark; Sourmash ships with no default phage database. Sketch parameters k=21, scaled=100 (search at k=21)

training_database: POG + VOG HMM profiles (Roux et al., 2015)
description: Probabilistic classifier that scans contigs for phage hallmark HMMs and assigns one of six confidence categories.
algorithmic_approach: Probabilistic modelling over Pfam/POG/VOG HMM profiles with reference and non-reference dependencies.
rationale_for_inclusion: Historical reference point: the first widely adopted metagenomic phage-identification tool (Roux et al., 2015) still in use and required for backward-comparable evaluations.
non_default_flags: -db 2 (Viromes reference database); the developer default is -db 1 (RefSeqABVir). Virome decontamination mode (--virome) was NOT enabled

training_database: RefSeq bacterial + viral pre-2014 (Ren et al., 2017)
description: K-mer-based logistic classifier that distinguishes phage from bacterial contigs using nucleotide composition.
algorithmic_approach: Logistic regression over 8-mer frequencies trained on RefSeq bacterial and viral genomes.
rationale_for_inclusion: Represents the first-generation sequence-composition tool that preceded the CNN era (Ren et al., 2017).

training_database: dsDNAphage + ssDNA + NCLDV + RNA + Lavidaviridae HMMs (Guo et al., 2021)
description: Multi-classifier that combines hallmark-gene HMMs with random-forest scoring across five viral groups (dsDNA phage/Caudovirales, ssDNA, NCLDV, RNA, Lavidaviridae).
algorithmic_approach: Random-forest ensembles per viral group over HMM hallmark-gene features and genomic-composition signals.
rationale_for_inclusion: Current community standard for broad-host-range viral identification and the top-ranked tool on aquatic benchmarks (Guo et al., 2021; Hegarty et al., 2024).
non_default_flags: Published-results runs used --provirus-off (provirus boundary detection disabled); the developer default enables it. Default group inclusion (dsDNAphage, ssDNA) retained. A control re-run with provirus boundary detection enabled (developer default; sample UC093_V3, 9 Tier 1 prophage contigs) recovered the identical prophage set (9/9 under both settings; overall MCC 0.365 vs 0.368, call differences confined to free-phage contigs), this single-sample check does not establish equivalence of the two settings across the full benchmark. The pipeline script (scripts/06_tool_execution/run_cpu_tools.sh) has been updated to run the developer default for future work.

training_database: KEGG + Pfam + VOG HMM profiles (Kieft et al., 2020)
description: Hybrid pipeline that combines HMM-based protein annotation with a neural network that classifies contigs as high-, medium-, or low-quality viral.
algorithmic_approach: Feed-forward neural network over KEGG, Pfam, and VOG HMM annotation profiles with viral-quality tiering.
rationale_for_inclusion: Broadly adopted tool that also reports viral quality tier and functional annotation, making it a natural precision-oriented comparator (Kieft et al., 2020).
non_default_flags: None: standard (non-virome) mode, default minimum length 1,000 bp and minimum ORFs = 4, bundled KEGG/Pfam/VOG databases passed explicitly via -k/-p/-v. Runtime logs report VIBRANT v1.0.1 despite the container tag 0.5.

training_database: RefSeq viral + bacterial pre-May 2015 (training pre-Jan 2014; validation Jan 2014–May 2015), augmented with metavirome sequences (Ren et al., 2020)
description: Convolutional neural network that classifies contigs based on raw nucleotide sequence without requiring ORF calling.
algorithmic_approach: Multi-layer CNN over one-hot-encoded nucleotide input trained on RefSeq viral and bacterial sequences (training cutoff May 2015), augmented with metavirome sequences for under-represented viral groups.
rationale_for_inclusion: Canonical first-generation deep-learning viral classifier and a standard benchmark for whether CNN architectures transfer to novel biomes (Ren et al., 2020).
non_default_flags: None (no -l length filter; score/p-value thresholding applied downstream at evaluation)

training_database: RefSeq viral + plasmid + chromosome (Fang et al., 2019)
description: Bi-path convolutional network that simultaneously classifies contigs as phage, plasmid, or chromosomal.
algorithmic_approach: Bi-path CNN (BiPathCNN) with a base path over nucleotide one-hot encoding and a codon path over codon one-hot encoding, trained on RefSeq viral, plasmid, and chromosomal sequences.
rationale_for_inclusion: Only benchmarked tool whose scope explicitly includes plasmids; important control for distinguishing phage from mobile genetic elements in CST-IV communities (Fang et al., 2019).

training_database: RefSeq phages + random bacterial fragments (Auslander et al., 2020)
description: LSTM-based neural classifier trained to distinguish phage from bacterial contigs without gene-level annotation.
algorithmic_approach: LSTM over nucleotide sequence with alignment-free phage vs bacterial discrimination.
rationale_for_inclusion: Represents the recurrent-network architecture class and provides a phage-only deep-learning baseline (Auslander et al., 2020).

training_database: RefSeq bacteria/archaea/eukaryotes + INPHARED phages (Wijesekara et al., 2024)
description: Deep-learning classifier operating on six-frame amino-acid translations of metagenome-assembled contigs for phage identification.
algorithmic_approach: Dilated CNN with residual connections (DCNN-Res; 28 layers, ~947K parameters) over six-frame amino-acid translations with learnable embeddings.
rationale_for_inclusion: Newest protein-translation-based classifier reported to recover short novel phage sequence where homology- and marker-based tools fail (Wijesekara et al., 2024).
non_default_flags: None (--batch 96 performance only; default classifier; sequences <2,048 bp silently skipped)

description: Multi-modal deep-learning classifier combining an LSTM over nucleotide sequence (HVSeeker-DNA) with a ProteinBERT fine-tuning branch over translated proteins (HVSeeker-Protein) to distinguish bacterial from phage sequences.
algorithmic_approach: Two-branch architecture: HVSeeker-DNA (LSTM over nucleotide sequence) + HVSeeker-Protein (ProteinBERT fine-tuned on protein sequences); scores integrated at contig level.
rationale_for_inclusion: Represents the multi-modal (DNA + protein) deep-learning class with a phage-specific training corpus, enabling protein-informed short-contig classification.
non_default_flags: Custom hvseeker_wrapper.py runs HVSeeker-DNA on fixed 500-bp windows (--min-length 500 --max-length 500 --threshold 0.5); HVSeeker provides no native CLI for variable-length metagenomic contigs, so contig-level scores are aggregated across 500-bp tiles by the wrapper

training_database: DNABERT-2 backbone; fungi, protozoa, insects as eukaryotic negatives (Peng et al., 2024)
description: Transformer-based language model fine-tuned to classify 2 kb nucleotide windows as viral or non-viral without ORF calling.
algorithmic_approach: DNABERT-2 backbone with task-specific fine-tuning; eukaryotic negatives (fungi, protozoa, insects) included in training.
rationale_for_inclusion: Includes fungi, protozoa and insects among its non-viral training examples; evaluates nucleotide-language-model classification on the short-fragment and eukaryote-infecting virus panels (Peng et al., 2024).
non_default_flags: None (default viralm predict; HuggingFace cache redirected via HF_HOME for offline execution)

training_database: RefSeq viral genomes (NCBI Virus, pre-October 2023; n = 15,037) + RefSeq host genomes from NCBI virus–host interaction tables (Wang et al., 2024)
description: Transformer-with-graph-inductive-network hybrid classifier that encodes contigs as graph-ordered k-mer windows.
algorithmic_approach: Graph inductive-network attention model over k-mer sequence windows trained on viral and cellular contigs.
rationale_for_inclusion: Represents the graph-attention architecture class; included to distinguish attention-based performance from generic transformer effects (Wang et al., 2024).
non_default_flags: Custom transginmer_wrapper.py invokes the native model with --threshold 0.5 and --min-length 100; default GNN scoring otherwise

training_database: GenBank (retrieved 6 July 2021) + IMG/VR v3 + curated genome sets (NCLDV, Leviviridae, Asgard archaea viruses, archaeal tailed viruses, Orthornavirae) + 227,897-profile marker library (Camargo et al., 2024)
description: Hybrid pipeline combining a sequence-based deep-learning branch with a curated marker-gene branch, integrated at contig level to classify virus, plasmid, or host.
algorithmic_approach: Two-branch model: IGLOO-based encoder (a convolution-attention hybrid architecture explicitly contrasted with CNNs and RNNs in the original paper) over nucleotide sequence plus HMM-style search against a 227,897-profile marker library; integration via score aggregation.
rationale_for_inclusion: State-of-the-art all-virus classifier; geNomad v1.11.0 was used to construct the MetaVR release (the IMG/VR v4 successor; Fiamenghi et al., 2026). Natural precision anchor for the benchmark (Camargo et al., 2024).
non_default_flags: None: genomad end-to-end with --cleanup; virus_score >= 0.7 is applied to reported whole-contig and region calls; no additional whole-parent score gate is imposed
